title: Stefan Kainbacher. Trialogue: Holobiont Habitat – Chapter 1. Decode
location:
Kunstraum Engländerbau (Lageplan)
Städtle 37
9490 Vaduz
Fürstentum Liechtenstein, Vaduz
description:
An expansive audiovisual installation about the possibilities and limits of communication between biological and technical actors.

Trialogue: Holobiont Habitat – Chapter 1: Decode is an expansive audiovisual installation about the possibilities and limits of communication between biological and technical actors.

In the center of the art space are eight black 19-inch server racks, arranged in a circle like a technological Stonehenge. The racks form the habitat of a hybrid organism in which plants, sensors, computers, artificial intelligence and audiovisual systems are connected.

Each rack houses live plants, full-spectrum grow lights, speakers, and various technical components. Network cables, power lines and hoses of an automated irrigation system connect the individual units into a common circuit. The technical infrastructure deliberately remains visible and becomes part of the spatial composition.

The plants are continuously recorded using various sensors. The focus is on measuring bioelectrical signals using Plant SpikerBox systems, supplemented by environmental and climate data. Four of the experimental stations also have camera systems with which the plants can be visually observed.

The collected data is processed by a locally operated multi-agent system. The AI ​​agents analyze electrical activity patterns, image data and environmental parameters and try to recognize connections, states and recurring patterns in the behavior of the plants. The installation stages this process not as a solved problem, but as an ongoing attempt at a machine approach to a non-human form of communication.

The work is seen as an artistic research setting: The AI ​​does not try to control plants, but rather to understand them. The actual topic of the work is less the plant itself and more the question of how technical systems create meaning and what limits exist.

Trialogue: Holobiont Habitat – Chapter 1: Decode marks the first part of an ongoing series of works. While this chapter addresses the question of decoding biological signals, future chapters will examine additional forms of interaction, translation, and coexistence between human and non-human actors.

title: State holiday - host community
description:
Host community on the national holiday 2026: We invite you to celebrate
On August 15, 2026, our community will be dedicated to the Liechtenstein state holiday. After mass in Bendern Church and the official state ceremony in Vaduz, visitors can look forward to a colorful festival program for the whole family from midday on Peter-Kaiser-Platz.
The Liechtenstein national holiday will be a special occasion for our community. As a host community, we actively participate in the celebrations and warmly invite the population and guests to experience this traditional holiday together.
The day begins at 8 a.m. with the solemn mass in Bendern Church. The musical accompaniment is provided exclusively by the organ. The service ends at around 8:45 a.m. before the participants set off together to Vaduz at 9 a.m. The official state ceremony begins there at 10:30 a.m. Tickets are required to attend the state ceremony. The ticket contingent at the municipality of Gamprin has already been exhausted. Further information on this can be found at staatsferientag.li.
From 12 p.m., Peter-Kaiser-Platz will be transformed into a lively meeting place for young and old. Six clubs from the community are looking forward to welcoming visitors: the volunteer fire department, the boy scouts, the ski club, the Gampriner Buschmönschterle, the Konkordia music club and the BIZLadies. Together, the clubs ensure a varied culinary offering of food and drinks.
The entertainment program also promises a varied afternoon. A bouncy castle and adhesive tattoos are available for children and families. The festival is complemented by a special stage program put together by the cultural commission.
With the diverse offering, Gamprin wants to make the national holiday a sociable and connecting experience for the entire community.

title: Finissage | In the context of the collection: RELAX (chiarenza & hauser & co)
location:
Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein (Lageplan)
Städtle 32
9490 Vaduz
Fürstentum Liechtenstein, Vaduz
description:
Guided tour and conversation with Christiane Meyer-Stoll and RELAX (chiarenza & hauser & co)
In cooperation with the Liechtenstein Art Society.

Marie-Antoinette Chiarenza (born 1957 in Tunis, TN) and Daniel Hauser (born 1959 in Bern, CH) have been working together since 1983 - since 1997 under the programmatic name RELAX.
The name stands for an attitude that suspends speed, pressure of expectation and tension and creates space for reflection and fundamental questions.

RELAX mostly work situation-related and take into account both the exhibition location and social, political, economic and ecological contexts. Her multimedia works question social values ​​as well as the canon and structures of art. With fine humor and an inquiring eye, RELAX opens up new perspectives: your room installation What is wealth? (2010–2017) from the collection of the Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein forms the starting point for further thoughts about value, possession, responsibility, memory - and happiness.

Works by RELAX have already given the title to exhibitions at the museum twice: Who pays? (2006) 2017 and What do we want to keep? (2018) 2021. With such open questions or groundbreaking statements, RELAX calls for thinking together - because thinking alone is criminal.

The exhibition What is wealth? was created in close collaboration with RELAX (chiarenza & hauser & co). She combines her works from the collection with a series of works created specifically for this solo presentation.

A production by the Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein, curated by Christiane Meyer-Stoll with Leslie Ospelt.

description:
Guided tour and conversation with Christiane Meyer-Stoll and RELAX (chiarenza & hauser & co)
In cooperation with the Liechtenstein Art Society.

Marie-Antoinette Chiarenza (born 1957 in Tunis, TN) and Daniel Hauser (born 1959 in Bern, CH) have been working together since 1983 - since 1997 under the programmatic name RELAX.
The name stands for an attitude that suspends speed, pressure of expectation and tension and creates space for reflection and fundamental questions.

RELAX mostly work situation-related and take into account both the exhibition location and social, political, economic and ecological contexts. Her multimedia works question social values ​​as well as the canon and structures of art. With fine humor and an inquiring eye, RELAX opens up new perspectives: your room installation What is wealth? (2010–2017) from the collection of the Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein forms the starting point for further thoughts about value, possession, responsibility, memory - and happiness.

Works by RELAX have already given the title to exhibitions at the museum twice: Who pays? (2006) 2017 and What do we want to keep? (2018) 2021. With such open questions or groundbreaking statements, RELAX calls for thinking together - because thinking alone is criminal.

The exhibition What is wealth? was created in close collaboration with RELAX (chiarenza & hauser & co). She combines her works from the collection with a series of works created specifically for this solo presentation.

A production by the Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein, curated by Christiane Meyer-Stoll with Leslie Ospelt.

description:
Pulsating rhythms, quick-witted virtuosity and sophisticated sounds: a concert for everyone who wants to leave everyday life behind them in a relaxed atmosphere after work.

Anyone who thinks of timpani and snare drums when they hear the term percussion will definitely be surprised this evening: the focus is on the marimba - an instrument with an expressive power that can best be described as voluminous resonance in all registers. At this after work concert, Christoph Sietzen and Bogdan Bacanu take the audience right into the heart of pulsating rhythms, quick-witted virtuosity and sophisticated sounds. The two artists have been making music together for many years. What they have in common is not only exceptional technical precision, but above all their playful lightness and great stage presence. “Pure Percussion” is a concert for the curious – for lovers of classical music as well as for everyone who wants to leave everyday life behind them in a relaxed atmosphere after work.

location:

description:
This evening's musical menu includes French sophistication, Italian passion and a touch of Argentine melancholy.

A good menu does not depend on a single course, but on the successful composition. It surprises, arouses curiosity and unfolds its charm from aisle to aisle. It's the same with this concert. The Ensemble Capucelli serves a little bit of everything – although not on plates, but with seven cellos. With Gautier Capuçon and the Ensemble Capucelli, seven outstanding cellists will be on stage. The ensemble was created through Capuçon's commitment to promoting young talent and brings together former award winners of his support program. Together, the seven cellists develop an ensemble sound that is as homogeneous as it is colorful and impressively show how versatile the cello is - as a solo instrument, as a chamber music partner and as a sound body of almost orchestral fullness. Rossini's "William Tell", Tchaikovsky's "Waltz of the Flowers", Ravel's "Boléro" or Piazzolla's "La muerte del ángel" are heard in arrangements specially created for cello ensembles and open up new perspectives on well-known masterpieces. A concert full of sonic discoveries: varied, surprising and with a pinch of French elegance.

Catching Flies is a British multi-instrumentalist and DJ. With synthesizers and a string quartet, he transforms the café in the art museum into a mixture of nightclub and concert hall.

Behind the name “Catching Flies” is the British multi-instrumentalist, producer and DJ George King. His music moves effortlessly between electronic beats and acoustic sound worlds. Warm synthesizer sounds meet strings, finely interwoven rhythms meet catchy melodies. “Catching Flies” is known for its unmistakably warm and atmospheric sound. His tracks combine atmospheric electronics with complex rhythms and range from hip-hop to house to soul and jazz. Together with his British string quartet, he transforms the CAFE in the art museum into a mixture of urban nightclub and stylish concert hall. “Catching Flies” has impressively proven in recent years that this connection is much more than an exciting experiment. His recent highlights include a BBC Radio 1 Essential Mix, a live video with the string quartet for Anjunadeep, one of the most famous electronic music labels in the world, and a live performance of his track “Orsay” at the Musée d’Orsay in Paris. A concert to listen to, immerse yourself in and take part in: atmospherically dense and sonically sophisticated – the perfect soundtrack for a long festival night.

At this after work concert, Christoph Sietzen and Bogdan Bacanu take the audience right into the heart of pulsating rhythms, quick-witted virtuosity and sophisticated sounds. Take a seat, lean back and enjoy the most beautiful melodies of opera literature right in the heart of Liechtenstein.

On this summer evening, the Vaduz town hall square is transformed into an open-air opera stage - with a backdrop that no set designer in the world could create. Because as soon as the sun slowly disappears behind the mountains and the first notes sound, the music unfolds its very special magic. Two of the most important opera stars of our time contribute to this: the soprano Nadine Sierra and the tenor Javier Camarena, who delight audiences at the world's major opera houses. After joint successes in Verdi's "La traviata" and Gounod's "Roméo et Juliette", they can now be experienced for the first time at VADUZ CLASSIC and give us an unforgettable evening with arias and duets full of passion, virtuosity and emotions. description:
This evening's musical menu includes French sophistication, Italian passion and a touch of Argentine melancholy.

A good menu does not depend on a single course, but on the successful composition. It surprises, arouses curiosity and unfolds its charm from aisle to aisle. It's the same with this concert. The Ensemble Capucelli serves a little bit of everything – although not on plates, but with seven cellos. With Gautier Capuçon and the Ensemble Capucelli, seven outstanding cellists will be on stage. The ensemble was created through Capuçon's commitment to promoting young talent and brings together former award winners of his support program. Together, the seven cellists develop an ensemble sound that is as homogeneous as it is colorful and impressively show how versatile the cello is - as a solo instrument, as a chamber music partner and as a sound body of almost orchestral fullness. Rossini's "William Tell", Tchaikovsky's "Waltz of the Flowers", Ravel's "Boléro" or Piazzolla's "La muerte del ángel" are heard in arrangements specially created for cello ensembles and open up new perspectives on well-known masterpieces. A concert full of sonic discoveries: varied, surprising and with a pinch of French elegance.

Behind the name “Catching Flies” is the British multi-instrumentalist, producer and DJ George King. His music moves effortlessly between electronic beats and acoustic sound worlds. Warm synthesizer sounds meet strings, finely interwoven rhythms meet catchy melodies. “Catching Flies” is known for its unmistakably warm and atmospheric sound. Chill & Thrill combines virtuosity, humor and improvisation. Aleksey Igudesman and Lucy Landymore surprise with Mozart and Latin American rhythms. A concert for the whole family.

The “Chill & Thrill” program delivers what the title promises. Virtuosity meets humor, improvisation meets sophisticated arrangements - and hardly a moment turns out the way you expect it. With Aleksey Igudesman you never know exactly what will happen next. One minute you're listening to the sounds of Mozart, but a few moments later Latin American rhythms create a South American spirit. Aleksey Igudesman has been one of the most original violinists and composers on the international music scene for many years. With his legendary duo Igudesman & Joo, he thrilled millions of audiences worldwide. Together with the British multi-instrumentalist, composer and percussionist Lucy Landymore, he is now presenting a program full of musical surprises. Own compositions alternate with sophisticated arrangements, quiet and atmospheric moments with virtuoso improvisations and rousing grooves. Laughter isn't always expected in concerts - but with Aleksey Igudesman and Lucy Landymore it's a given.

location:

Fürstentum Liechtenstein, Vaduz
description:
Two musicians who don't need a grand gesture to fill a room: with trumpet and double bass, Brönner & Ilg transform the art museum into a stage for subtle dialogue and virtuoso playing.

A summer evening in Vaduz and two musicians who don't need a big gesture to fill a room: When Till Brönner and Dieter Ilg perform together, two characters meet who support, challenge and push each other forward. Both musicians share the ability to not only tell stories, but to create them in the moment. Sometimes it seems like a quiet conversation late in the evening, sometimes like a spontaneous improvisation that only takes shape during the game. They don't rush from climax to climax, but rather give the music time to breathe. It is precisely where music leaves space and is not filled every second that the greatest tension often arises. Miles Davis repeatedly emphasized that the unplayed notes in jazz have at least the same meaning as those actually played. «The hearing is apparently capable of thinking about what cannot be heard. And according to our experience and our feelings, that really stimulates the brain and the heart,” says Till Brönner. This is exactly what makes this duo so attractive. The music never seems overloaded or demonstrative, but rather clear, concentrated and open.

description:
A production by the Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein, curated by Annett Höland.

Evi Kliemand (born 1946) is a painter, writer, poet, journalist and art educator.

The exhibition takes the artist's works from the collection of the Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein as a starting point and makes some of her creative phases tangible.

In addition to Kliemand's painting work, his photographic work is present in picture cycles, supplemented by insights into his graphic work. Poetic sequences and poems from the audio book editions make the written work audible. In addition, works from the recent past reveal a multidimensional reality.

In the artist's words: "In search of what is disappearing, what is missing, what has not become visible - what has been passed over and destroyed - by which the senses are touched as those affected, what is perceived at the door. As if she were walking on water, she stood on the shore of her painting.”

location:
Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein (Lageplan)
Städtle 32
9490 Vaduz
Fürstentum Liechtenstein, Vaduz
description:
with Christiane Meyer-Stoll

For over 50 years, Eleanor Antin (born 1935 in New York, USA) has been one of the groundbreaking voices of her generation.

As a pioneer of artistic self-staging, she creates and embodies fictional characters and thus asks central questions about identity, history and representation. Her work combines profound humor with subtle storytelling. Antin's cross-media practice - photography, film, text, performance, sculpture and installation - invites us to take a new look at familiar narratives and discover amazing perspectives on our individual and social self-image.

Since the late 1960s, Antin has explored the fluid existence of the self. She slips into different roles – the king, the ballerina or the nurse – that carry different identities, historical references and internal contradictions.

This retrospective highlights the complexity of Antin's oeuvre and shows how relevant and impactful her work remains today.

Curated for the Liechtenstein Art Museum by Christiane Meyer-Stoll with Henrik Utermöhle. The exhibition was initiated and organized by Mudam Luxembourg – Musée d'Art Moderne Grand-Duc Jean. After Vaduz, the exhibition travels to the MOCAK – Museum of Contemporary Art in Krakow.

The exhibition is accompanied by the publication Eleanor Antin. Works 1965–2017 and the Edition 2 Boots (after Eleanor Antin) (2026) by Manfred Naescher, which was created specifically for the Liechtenstein Art Museum.

description:
TAK Vaduz world classic concerts

Andriy Dragan rediscovers the fascinating sound world of Franz Xaver Mozart. An exciting intergenerational dialogue emerges between two of his father's masterpieces - with Bogdan Božović and the Winterthur Music College.

It was both a blessing and a curse for Franz Xaver Mozart to follow in his famous father's footsteps as a composer and pianist. His compositional work shows an independent musical signature - and yet always remained in the shadow of his overpowering father.

The Swiss-Ukrainian pianist Andriy Dragan is one of the few soloists who takes on Franz Xaver Mozart's little-known repertoire with a keen sense of flair.

Framed by two works by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, the program spans an arc between early lightness and mature mastery. Bogdan Božović leads the Musikkollegium Winterthur through this dialogue between generations from the podium and as a soloist in Mozart's fifth violin concerto.

title: ParkingDay 2026 - Circular Economy in Vaduz
location:
Vadozner Huus (Lageplan)
Städtle 14
9490 Vaduz
Fürstentum Liechtenstein, Vaduz
description:
What happens to our waste after we throw it away? Which materials can be recycled, what can be reused and how can we avoid waste from the start?

During Parking Day 2026, parking spaces in the Vaduz Städtle will be transformed into an interactive experience space around the circular economy in Vaduz for two days. The Sustainability Commission of the municipality of Vaduz clearly shows what happens to our recyclable materials and how we can all help keep resources in circulation for longer.

The exhibition makes visible what otherwise often remains hidden: How much waste is generated per person? What can be reused or recycled? Which materials are often disposed of incorrectly? And what influence does our consumer behavior have on the environment and resources?

The parking area becomes a mirror of our everyday life. It shows which recyclable materials can be collected, reused or recycled and makes it clear that supposed waste often still contains valuable raw materials. Because one thing is clear: thrown away does not automatically mean disappeared.

In addition to exciting information about recycling, reuse, reusability and sustainable consumption, visitors can also expect insights into local initiatives and projects that are committed to a functioning circular economy.

The Vadozer Huus offers creative, hands-on activities for families and children. When crafting with reused materials, new ideas for old things arise and you can also experience how reuse conserves resources.

Our message: The best waste is the one that isn't created in the first place. But we can also make a big difference when it comes to unavoidable waste. Anyone who consumes consciously, separates them correctly and uses products for as long as possible helps to keep valuable raw materials in circulation and make the future more sustainable.

Parking Day is an international campaign in which parking spaces are temporarily converted for one or several days. Instead of cars, the focus is on people, encounters, creativity and sustainable ideas. Public parking areas become places of exchange, information and experience. The aim is to create new perspectives on the use of public space and to draw attention to socially relevant issues.

title: Baby & Job?! - Childcare in FL/CH/A
description:
Find out all about childcare options in Liechtenstein, Switzerland and Vorarlberg. Here you will get practical tips to successfully reconcile family and work.

Even during pregnancy, it is important to deal with the question of child care. If you work in Liechtenstein or Switzerland, you need child care for the baby even earlier.

During the presentation, you will receive useful information and tips on the following topics. Afterwards we are happy to answer further questions.

• What care options are available for babies and toddlers?
• Where can I find the right points of contact for my questions?
• How can I deal with the pressure to organize everything in time?
• What helps me get into the moment and build a loving connection with my child?

Our online presentation provides valuable information about childcare options in Liechtenstein, Switzerland and Vorarlberg. We show you ways to master the balancing act between family and work – with practical tips for a mindful pregnancy and parental leave.

Through this online lecture, our consultants lead Bettina Eberle-Frommelt, psychologist and psychotherapist with professional experience in the child care sector and Elke Oswald-Öksüz, psychologist and relaxation coach, who is still a toddler mom.

The online presentation and subsequent questionnaire session lasts about 1 hour. It is free and held via Zoom. You will receive the corresponding link after your registration. We look forward to your participation.

Registration takes place via the pregnancy.li website or via the registration link on the right.

In the 18th century, P. Schmid worked with the Chiquitos in present-day Bolivia. Through his work, music became a connecting language of faith, community and encounter between cultures. His compositions testify to the fruitful interplay between European Baroque tradition and local music culture.

title: “It doesn’t work without love” Silvia Ruppen’s stamp art
location:
Liechtensteinisches PostMuseum (Lageplan)
Städtle 37
9490 Vaduz
Fürstentum Liechtenstein, Vaduz
description:
The exhibition invites you to take a close look and discover 25 years of stamps designed with heart and hand.

“It can’t be done without love.” Silvia Ruppen once wrote this sentence on one of her stamp sketches. He fits a designer who particularly likes to work by hand. With pen, brush and a lot of attention to detail, she creates her own visual worlds in the smallest space.

How many different topics fit on stamps is shown in this special exhibition with 49 stamps from the years 2001 to 2025: Sometimes tiny bees and other native animals are the focus, sometimes agriculture, sometimes science. In turn, precious jewellery eggs or masterpieces by Gustav Klimt and Peter Paul Rubens become the motif.

Each stamp presented Silvia Ruppen with a new task: How can a complex topic be condensed into a few square centimeters? How does this create an image that is curious and remains in the memory?

The exhibition invites you to take a close look and discover 25 years of stamps designed with heart and hand.

description:
TAK Vaduzer world classical concerts

Between sound art and environmental reflection, recycling becomes an instrument. Gregor Amadeus Mayrhofer’s Concerto transforms thrown things into music – interpreted by the expressive percussionist Vivi Vassileva.

Basically, a percussion concert is not only an acoustic, but also a visual experience. And not only since John Cage, the instrumentarium is often composed more of found items than of traditional instruments.

The Recycling Concerto by Munich composer Gregor Amadeus Mayrhofer is about more than just effects. Glass bottles and plastic bags, flower pots, a deposit bottle marimba and other recycling garbage combine here in the most exciting way with the orchestral instruments. The increasing littering of the environment is the musical theme of Mayrhofer in a highly multi-layered manner and provides the percussionist and the Symphony Orchestra Liechtenstein with a complex and entertaining stage.

Vivi Vassileva is an artist who misses and pushes the boundaries of percussion music anew and knows how to let the spark jump between work and audience. Not only is she celebrated for her brilliant technique, her stage performance is as athletic as it is charismatic.

Vivi Vassileva, Percussion

Werewolves. Kill them. Or they will kill you. It will be dark at the Creative Academy! “Werwolves – the Show” combines improvisational theater with the worldwide successful social play.

There is tranquil peace in Düsterwald, a small village in a remote valley. The tranquility is cruelly disturbed when a bloody curse hits the village. Some of the residents turn into werewolves at night and go hunting for people. Every night it meets another innocent victim. No one is safe anymore. During the day, the villagers try to expose and kill the werewolves. How do you recognize a werewolf? Who can be trusted and who made themselves suspect? Whether the mayor or his own wife – evil can slumber in everyone. The audience as a village court has the last word. Will the audience succeed in stopping the werewolves before it is finally too late for Düsterwald? An exciting race against time with (of course) a good portion of situation comedy. title: “It won’t work without love” Silvia Ruppen’s stamp art
location:
Liechtensteinisches PostMuseum (Lageplan)
Städtle 37
9490 Vaduz
Fürstentum Liechtenstein, Vaduz
description:
The exhibition invites you to take a close look and discover 25 years of stamps designed with heart and hand.

“It can’t be done without love.” Silvia Ruppen once wrote this sentence on one of her stamp sketches. He fits a designer who particularly likes to work by hand. With pen, brush and a lot of attention to detail, she creates her own visual worlds in the smallest space.

How many different topics fit on stamps is shown in this special exhibition with 49 stamps from the years 2001 to 2025: Sometimes tiny bees and other native animals are the focus, sometimes agriculture, sometimes science. In turn, precious jewellery eggs or masterpieces by Gustav Klimt and Peter Paul Rubens become the motif.

Each stamp presented Silvia Ruppen with a new task: How can a complex topic be condensed into a few square centimeters? How does this create an image that is curious and remains in the memory?

The exhibition invites you to take a close look and discover 25 years of stamps designed with heart and hand.

Anna Jermolaeva (born 1970 in St. Petersburg, RU) directs her watchful and empathetic gaze at everyday moments that are easily overlooked and transforms them into vivid parables for social and political realities. She often works in the settings of her own biography, especially in countries related to the former Soviet Union, where she lived until her escape in 1989.

Jermolaeva’s artistic practice includes video, installation, photography, performance, painting and sculpture. She is particularly interested in the subtle mechanisms of influence that shape our everyday life.

Anna Jermolaewa has already been represented in two group exhibitions at the Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein. Two works of the artist are in the collection; Both were part of their contribution to the Austrian Pavilion at the Venice Biennale in 2024. For her large solo exhibition, Jermolaeva will develop new works.

description:
TAK Vaduzer world classical concerts

Between sound art and environmental reflection, recycling becomes an instrument. Gregor Amadeus Mayrhofer’s Concerto transforms thrown things into music – interpreted by the expressive percussionist Vivi Vassileva.

Basically, a percussion concert is not only an acoustic, but also a visual experience. And not only since John Cage, the instrumentarium is often composed more of found items than of traditional instruments.

The Recycling Concerto by Munich composer Gregor Amadeus Mayrhofer is about more than just effects. Glass bottles and plastic bags, flower pots, a deposit bottle marimba and other recycling garbage combine here in the most exciting way with the orchestral instruments. Mayrhofer’s musical themes on the increasing littering of the environment are highly complex and provide the percussionist and the Liechtenstein Symphony Orchestra with a complex and entertaining stage.

Vivi Vassileva is an artist who misses and pushes the boundaries of percussion music anew and knows how to let the spark jump between work and audience. She is not only celebrated for her brilliant technique, her stage performance is as athletic as it is charismatic.

It will be dark at the Creative Academy! “Werwolves – the Show” combines improvisational theater with the worldwide successful social play.

Werewolves. Kill them. Or they will kill you. It will be dark at the Creative Academy! “Werwolves – the Show” combines improvisational theater with the worldwide successful social play.

There is tranquil peace in Düsterwald, a small village in a remote valley. The peace is cruelly disturbed when a bloody curse hits the village. Some of the residents turn into werewolves at night and go hunting for people. Every night it meets another innocent victim. No one is safe anymore. During the day, the villagers try to expose and kill the werewolves. How do you recognize a werewolf? Who can be trusted and who made themselves suspect? Whether the mayor or his own wife – evil can slumber in everyone. The audience as a village court has the last word. Will the audience succeed in stopping the werewolves before it is finally too late for Düsterwald? An exciting race against time with (of course) a good portion of situation comedy. Goosebumps guaranteed!
